d: SLIM (Scalable Lightweight Interactive Models) automatically generates optimized, cloud-transcoded representations of models and avatars for improved performance and visual quality.
h:
SLIM (Scalable Lightweight Interactive Models) is an automatic optimization system that generates lightweight, optimized representations of Models and platform avatars using cloud-based transcoding (converting assets into more efficient formats). When enabled, SLIM combines multiple parts into fewer draw calls (rendering commands sent to the GPU) and generates multiple levels of detail, allowing the engine to intelligently select the best representation based on distance, device capability, and available resources.

<figure>
    <img src="../../assets/optimization/streaming/SLIM-Disabled.jpg" />
    <figcaption>Without SLIM — streamed-out models are invisible</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure>
    <img src="../../assets/optimization/streaming/SLIM-Enabled.jpg" />
    <figcaption>With SLIM — optimized stand-ins remain visible</figcaption>
</figure>

SLIM provides three key benefits:

  • Visual quality — Distant models appear more detailed than the legacy model level‑of‑detail system, maintaining closer fidelity to the original.
  • Consistent transitions — All parts within a model switch detail levels simultaneously, eliminating jarring per-part transitions.
  • Performance — Composite meshes dramatically reduce draw calls, triangle counts, and memory usage, enabling richer scenes across all device tiers.

Explore SLIM in these published games:

Prerequisites

SLIM requires the following:

  1. StreamingEnabled must be enabled on the Workspace object. See also streaming properties for related recommended settings.
  2. The place must be saved to Roblox (not a local .rbxl file), as SLIM uses cloud transcoding to generate optimized assets. If you're testing locally, publish the place and then enable SLIM.
  3. Team Create must be enabled for the game, as SLIM relies on associated properties for cloud asset generation.

Technical behavior

When you publish or playtest a game with SLIM-enabled models, the engine uploads model data to a cloud service that generates optimized composite meshes with multiple levels of detail. At runtime, clients fetch these assets from the CDN and the engine selects the appropriate detail level based on distance and device capability, classifying each SLIM model into rendering zones based on distance from the camera:

Range Data Model State Rendering
Full instances streamed in. Traditional part-by-part rendering.
Full instances streamed in. The engine renders the SLIM composite when more efficient.
Instances streamed out. Only a minimal placeholder exists in the DataModel, not the full model hierarchy. SLIM composite rendering.
Minimal placeholder in the DataModel. Not rendered.

SLIM for models

SLIM works best on models that represent static world geometry — buildings, props, vehicles, terrain features, and other environment objects that don't change at/during runtime. Adding or removing parts, changing materials, or modifying geometry at runtime prevents SLIM from rendering the model correctly. See model structure for general model structure guidance and limitations for the full list of exclusions.

To enable SLIM on a model, set its LevelOfDetail property to SLIM in the Properties window.

When SLIM is set on a model, the engine:

  1. Serializes the model's rendering-relevant properties (geometry, materials, textures, transforms) into a compact representation. Supported instance types within the model include Part, MeshPart, Decal, Texture, SurfaceAppearance, PartOperation, NegateOperation, and SpecialMesh.
  2. Uploads this data to the cloud transcoding service on first publish or play.
  3. The cloud service generates a composited mesh with multiple levels of detail, removing hidden internal geometry and optimizing textures.
  4. At runtime, clients fetch the optimized SLIM asset and render it when the engine streams out the original model or when SLIM is more efficient than the full model.

Initial SLIM generation might take a few moments for complex models. The cloud service processes assets in the background, so if a model doesn't appear as SLIM immediately after enabling, wait 1–2 minutes and rejoin; the transcoded asset persists on the CDN and the client fetches it on the next session.

Converting from Streaming Mesh

If your game uses the legacy StreamingMesh setting for Model.LevelOfDetail, you can convert individual models by selecting them and changing the property in the Properties window, or you can batch-convert multiple models at once using a script like the following in the Command Bar. Note that some models which worked with StreamingMesh might need adjustments for SLIM, particularly those with overlapping parts or complex PartOperation hierarchies.

Batch-Convert StreamingMesh to SLIM

for _, descendant in workspace:GetDescendants() do
    if descendant:IsA("Model") and descendant.LevelOfDetail ==
        Enum.ModelLevelOfDetail.StreamingMesh then
        descendant.LevelOfDetail = Enum.ModelLevelOfDetail.SLIM
    end
end

SLIM for avatars

Platform avatars outside of the currently streamed area are not visible by default. Enabling SLIM avatars renders standard player characters — regardless of how many accessories or clothing layers they have — as lightweight, animated stand‑ins that maintain visual fidelity at a fraction of the rendering cost.

The key SLIM-specific property for avatars is Workspace.EnableSLIMAvatars which should be set to Enabled in the Properties window, alongside LevelOfDetail set to SLIM on your non‑avatar world models.

With EnableSLIMAvatars enabled, the engine:

  • Renders a SLIM version when an actual avatar model streams out.
  • Swaps between SLIM and full-resolution representations based on available resources, even inside the streaming radius.
  • Throttles SLIM animations based on scene importance and available bandwidth.

Supported Avatars

  • R15 avatars with a body, dynamic head, [standard](https://create.roblox.com/docs/avatar/character-bodies/specifications#standard-r15-rigs) or [advanced](https://create.roblox.com/docs/avatar/character-bodies/specifications#advanced-r15-rigs) R15 rig, and rigid/layered accessories.
  • Avatar changes made between the CharacterAdded event and CharacterAppearanceLoaded event.
**Excluded Avatars**
<ul>
<li>R6 avatars.</li>
<li>NPC characters (even those with a standard or advanced R15 rig).</li>
<li>Avatars with custom proportions, body scaling, or experience-applied avatar settings.</li>
<li>Avatar changes made after the CharacterAppearanceLoaded event (equipping tools, accessory changes, Highlight additions, etc.).</li>
</ul>
Testing SLIM Avatars

Unlike model SLIM which you can test alone by moving far from a model until it streams out, SLIM avatars require multiple players in the game to observe. Use one of these testing modes to test SLIM avatars:

  • Team Test — Join with friends or alternate accounts to see SLIM avatars at distance.
  • Server and Clients — Launch two or more client windows where each client displays avatar copies that the others render as SLIM when at distance.

Note that avatars must have been transcoded in a SLIM-enabled game before they appear as SLIM. If avatars don't render as SLIM in your first test, rejoin the game after a moment to allow transcoding to complete.

Limitations

Limitation Details
**Streaming required** SLIM only functions with StreamingEnabled set to `true`. Without streaming, SLIM‑eligible models fall back to traditional level‑of‑detail rendering.
**Static models only** [Model SLIM](#slim-for-models) does not support models modified at runtime (parts added/removed, properties changed) or models that play animations.
**Humanoid instances** The engine excludes models containing a Humanoid from static [model SLIM](#slim-for-models) processing. Use [SLIM avatars](#slim-for-avatars) for animated player characters.
**Avatar restrictions** [SLIM avatars](#slim-for-avatars) only support R15 player characters. R6 rigs, NPCs, and avatars with custom proportions fall back to default rendering.
**Cloud dependency** The cloud service generates and stores SLIM assets on the CDN. Offline or local testing without a published place does not produce SLIM results.
**Zero-scale models** The engine excludes models with a Scale of `0` from SLIM processing.
**Platform availability** On platforms where SLIM is not yet supported, models set to SLIM fall back to Disabled.

Debugging

To better understand the status of SLIM models, Roblox provides several debug tint modes in the DebugVisualizations ⟩ SlimTintMode dropdown of the Developer Console. Note that this menu is only available to creators who have Edit permissions for the game.

There are multiple tint modes to select from. See SlimTintMode for the color mappings of each mode.

LOD colors each mesh by its current level of detail using a blue-to-red heatmap. Blue indicates the lowest detail and warmer colors indicate higher detail.

DataModelState colors meshes by streaming state of the DataModel. Teal indicates the high-fidelity zone where the DataModel is present; yellow indicates the low-fidelity zone where the DataModel is absent.

You can also see SLIM debug visualizations in Studio by selecting a tint mode from the Visualization Options menu:

In addition to the LOD/DataModelState tint modes, Studio offers the TranscoderStatus tint mode. While editing, only this tint mode is available in the visualization options menu; while playing, all the tint modes are available. See SlimTranscoderStatus for the color mappings of each status.


Troubleshooting

SLIM model not appearing
  • Verify that StreamingEnabled is true.
  • Confirm the place is published to Roblox and Team Create is enabled.
  • Check that LevelOfDetail is set to SLIM for the model.
  • Wait 1–2 minutes after first publish for cloud transcoding to complete, then rejoin.
  • Ensure the model doesn't contain a Humanoid instance.
Solid modeling operations not rendering correctly in SLIM

PartOperation instances for solid modeling (unions, intersections, negations) might not render correctly in some SLIM models. If a union appears missing or distorted in the SLIM representation, try separating the affected PartOperation into its own model or simplifying the CSG operation.

Z-fighting or flickering on SLIM models

Z-fighting can occur when parts in the original model have overlapping or coplanar faces. To resolve:

  • Move overlapping parts slightly apart (even 0.01 studs is sufficient).
  • Avoid perfectly flush surfaces between adjacent parts in the same model.
Texture or UV shifts on SLIM models

SLIM regenerates UV mappings (how textures are projected onto 3D surfaces) during transcoding. Default Roblox materials might show slightly different tiling patterns compared to the original. To mitigate:

  • Use custom textures via SurfaceAppearance for important surfaces.
  • Group visually related parts into the same model to ensure consistent texturing.
SLIM avatars not rendering
  • Verify Workspace.EnableSLIMAvatars is set to Enabled.
  • Test with multiple clients using Server and Clients test mode (requires at least 2 clients).
  • Ensure the avatar uses a standard or advanced R15 rig without custom proportions.
  • Confirm the game doesn't modify the avatar after the Player.CharacterAppearanceLoaded event.
Visual glitches on animated SLIM avatars

Full-body or finger animations might occasionally show visual artifacts due to bone replication timing. This is a known issue being actively improved. If the issue is severe, verify that animation scripts aren't modifying bone transforms outside of the standard animation pipeline.

Inaccurate triangle count in rendering stats

The rendering stats panel might report incorrect triangle counts when SLIM avatars are enabled. This is a known reporting bug and does not affect actual rendering performance.

kid.simple: SLIM is a Roblox feature that makes cheap, good-looking stand-ins for models and player avatars that are far away. With streaming on, faraway things normally vanish because they are not loaded. With SLIM, Roblox's cloud builds a light version that still shows up, so your city skyline or crowd of players does not just disappear. It also makes games run faster, because the stand-in costs much less for the device to draw.
kid.analogy: It is like a cardboard cutout of a building on a movie set. From far away it looks just like the real building, but it is light and cheap. When the camera walks close, the real building is swapped in.
keyPoints: SLIM needs three things: StreamingEnabled on, the place saved to Roblox (not just a local file), and Team Create turned on.
To use SLIM on a model, set its `LevelOfDetail` property to SLIM in the Properties window.
SLIM works best on models that never change while the game runs, like buildings, props, and scenery. Adding parts, changing materials, or animating breaks it.
Models with a Humanoid inside are skipped. For player characters, set `Workspace.EnableSLIMAvatars` to Enabled instead.
SLIM avatars only work for R15 player characters with normal proportions. R6 avatars and NPCs are not included.
In one example crowd far away, SLIM cut about 2,600,000 triangles down to about 170,000.
The first time, the cloud may need 1 to 2 minutes to build the SLIM version. Wait, then rejoin.
Debug tint modes in the Developer Console and Studio's Visualization Options color models so you can see their SLIM status.

terms.SLIM: Scalable Lightweight Interactive Models. Roblox's system for making light, faraway versions of models and avatars.
terms.transcoding: Converting something into a different, more efficient format. Roblox's cloud transcodes your model into a SLIM mesh.
terms.draw call: One instruction sent to the graphics chip to draw something. Fewer draw calls means a faster game. SLIM can draw a 50-part house in far fewer calls.
terms.GPU: The graphics chip in a device that draws everything on screen.
terms.triangle: The tiny flat shapes every 3D model is built from. Fewer triangles means less work for the device.
terms.composite mesh: Many parts merged into one single mesh.
terms.level of detail: Using simpler versions of objects the farther away they are.
terms.fidelity: How close something looks to the real original.
terms.CDN: A network of servers around the world that stores files, like SLIM assets, so players can download them quickly.
terms.static: Not changing while the game runs.
terms.R15 / R6: Two kinds of Roblox character bodies. R15 has 15 body parts and R6 has 6.
terms.z-fighting: Flickering when two surfaces sit in exactly the same spot and the game cannot decide which to show. Moving one by even 0.01 studs fixes it.
terms.UV mapping: Instructions for how a flat image wraps around a 3D shape.

example.title: Turn on SLIM for every model in a Buildings folder
example.place: Studio Command Bar (View > Command Bar), run once while editing a published place with streaming and Team Create on
example.code:
-- Find the folder that holds all the static buildings
local buildings = workspace:FindFirstChild("Buildings")

if buildings then
	local count = 0
	for _, item in buildings:GetDescendants() do
		-- Only models that are not characters (no Humanoid inside)
		if item:IsA("Model") and not item:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("Humanoid", true) then
			item.LevelOfDetail = Enum.ModelLevelOfDetail.SLIM
			count += 1
		end
	end
	print("Set SLIM on " .. count .. " models")
else
	warn("No folder named Buildings in Workspace")
end
explain: The Command Bar runs code in Studio right away, which is handy for changing many objects at once.
We look for a folder called Buildings in Workspace, since only static scenery should use SLIM.
We go through everything inside it and pick out Models that have no Humanoid, because SLIM skips characters anyway.
We set each one's `LevelOfDetail` to SLIM and count them, then print the total so you know it worked.

watchOut: Testing SLIM in an unpublished local file. SLIM needs Roblox's cloud, so publish first and turn on Team Create.
Putting SLIM on doors, moving platforms, or animated models. SLIM is for things that never change during play.
Expecting to see SLIM avatars when testing alone. You need at least 2 clients, like Server and Clients test mode or a Team Test.
Changing a player's avatar after CharacterAppearanceLoaded (like adding a Highlight) and wondering why SLIM does not show it.
